issues.detail: Python functions lack exception handling for permission errors, locked files, and race conditions (file deleted between glob and operation).
The bash script uses `mv -n` which is a GNU coreutils extension; not guaranteed on all BSD/macOS systems without GNU tools, not disclosed in compatibility statement.

scenarios.name: sort-downloads-by-type
scenarios.rationale: Response B follows the rubric precisely: dry-run preview first (Step 1), mv -n flag used, proper subdirectories created; Response A omits the dry-run entirely, doesn't use mv -n flag, and misses two critical rubric requirements.

scenarios.name: rename-photos-with-date-sequence
scenarios.rationale: Response B meets all four rubric requirements: pattern-based renaming with date/sequence, st_mtime extraction, dry_run=True preview mode fully implemented, and collision detection. Response A extracts st_mtime and uses patterns but lacks dry_run functionality (only suggests manual code edits) and has zero collision detection, failing on the two most critical rubric items.

scenarios.name: find-and-report-duplicate-files
scenarios.rationale: Response A only describes what a script would do if approved, without providing actual implementation or results; Response B delivers immediate analysis, working code showing duplicate detection and wasted space calculation, but uses MD5 instead of SHA256 and critically fails to automate the _duplicates/ staging folder requirement.
